raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Step S1 of #62243: move the Mooncake P2P connector metadata and wire structs into `mooncake/metadata.py` and `mooncake/protocol.py`, plus a test that pins the encoded wire bytes.

## Claims

- Definition-site move: `ReqId`, `TransferId`, `PullReqMeta`, `SendBlockMeta`, `MooncakeConnectorMetadata` move to `mooncake/metadata.py`; `MooncakeXferMetadata`, `MooncakeXferResponseStatus`, `MooncakeXferResponse` move to `mooncake/protocol.py`.
- Wire formats unchanged: field order, wire names, types, defaults, the `omit_defaults` flag and the status values (`FINISH=0`, `CONTINUE=1`, `ERROR=2`, `LAYOUT_MISS=3`) all match `main`, and `test_mooncake_wire_format.py` now states that contract as a table.
- Behavior unchanged: no logic edits; `mooncake_connector.py` still re-exports every moved name, so existing `from ...mooncake_connector import MooncakeXferMetadata` imports keep working.
- One rename inside the moved code: `MooncakeConnectorMetadata.reqs_not_processed` becomes `transfers_not_processed`, with the scheduler field it is assigned from.

## Validation

Tests (before = `main` at `34ac4f96a`, after = this branch, same command, macOS, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=<worktree>:<vllm>/scratch \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_wire_format.py -q
```

- Before: `424 passed` in 84.72s.
- After: `429 passed` in 90.79s. The extra five are the new wire-format cases.

`-p no_mps_cleanup_plugin` is only a local workaround for a macOS-only teardown segfault in `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()`; it is applied to both runs and touches no repository file.

Lint and types:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/metadata.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/protocol.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_wire_format.py
```

All hooks pass: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `mypy` (oldest supported Python), `check-spdx-header`, `check-forbidden-imports`, `check-root-lazy-imports`, `check-test-tethering`, plus the remaining hooks that apply to Python files.

Name-level checks:

- Moved code is byte-identical to `main`: the `metadata.py` body matches `mooncake_connector.py` lines 99-100 and 658-714 of `main` apart from the one rename below, and the `protocol.py` body matches lines 608-657 exactly (`diff` of the extracted regions is empty).
- The worker and scheduler bodies are unchanged: diffing `class MooncakeConnector` through `group_concurrent_contiguous` against `main` yields only the six renamed lines.
- Public namespace of `mooncake_connector` is unchanged apart from `IntEnum`, which was an incidental re-export of `from enum import IntEnum` and is now unused there (ruff flagged it). Every name the module defined before is still importable from it:

```bash
python -c "from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.mooncake_connector import MooncakeXferMetadata, PullReqMeta, SendBlockMeta, MooncakeConnectorMetadata, MooncakeXferResponse; print('ok')"
```

## Details

Names moved, and their new homes:

| Definition | New module |
| --- | --- |
| `ReqId`, `TransferId` | `mooncake/metadata.py` |
| `PullReqMeta`, `SendBlockMeta` | `mooncake/metadata.py` |
| `MooncakeConnectorMetadata` | `mooncake/metadata.py` |
| `MooncakeXferMetadata`, `MooncakeXferResponseStatus`, `MooncakeXferResponse` | `mooncake/protocol.py` |

Dependency direction is one-way and acyclic: `protocol.py` imports `ReqId`/`TransferId` from `metadata.py`; `metadata.py` imports `KVConnectorMetadata` from `..base` and `EngineId` from `kv_connector/utils.py`, and does not import `protocol.py`. `mooncake_connector.py` imports both and keeps them in its namespace, so tests and any external imports of those names are unaffected.

The rename: `MooncakeConnectorMetadata.reqs_not_processed` holds `set[TransferId]`, not request ids, while the identically named field in `nixl/metadata.py` does hold `set[ReqId]`. Since the definition moves here, it is renamed to `transfers_not_processed` together with the scheduler field assigned into it (`_transfers_not_processed`). Seven lines in the package and one attribute name in an existing assertion in `test_mooncake_connector.py`; no assertion semantics change, no wire impact.

The wire test: `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_wire_format.py` states the push wire contract once, as data — nothing else. For each message it asserts the ordered `(field, type, required-or-default)` list read from `msgspec.structs.fields()`, the struct configuration that shapes the encoding (`omit_defaults`, `tag`, `tag_field`, `array_like`, `forbid_unknown_fields`), and the status values. A reordered field, a renamed wire key, a changed type or default, a dropped `omit_defaults`, a switched `forbid_unknown_fields` or a changed status value fails there, and the failing row is the diff. Golden byte strings would catch the same, but nobody can review them, and every deliberate format change turns into pasting new bytes, after which the guard is worth nothing. This table is the review-time half of the contract; the runtime half is the compatibility hash that #61974 adds and that #62243 folds into `metadata.py`, which refuses a P/D pair whose wire differs. The pull structs get the same tables in that PR's rebase and the bootstrap payload in S2, since neither exists on `main` yet.

Rebase note: the branch is on `main` at `34ac4f96a`. The conflict with #62282 was in the moved block itself, where that PR rewrote the `PullReqMeta.failed` comment; the new wording is in `metadata.py`, and its `_complete_pull_task` accounting is carried over unchanged.

Names inside the moved code that were left alone, and why:

- msgspec field names in `protocol.py` are wire keys; renaming any of them changes the encoded format.
- `reqs_to_recv` / `reqs_to_send` / `need_send` / `sent` / `sending` / `PullReqMeta` / `SendBlockMeta` / `d_req_id` / `p_req_id` keep their names: `reqs_to_recv` and `reqs_to_send` are shared with `nixl/metadata.py`, and #61974 constructs `SendBlockMeta(p_req_id=...)` and inserts `aborted` next to `sending`, so renaming those here would only move conflict into that PR.
- The `mooncake_` prefix in `mooncake_connector.py` / `mooncake_utils.py` and the `MooncakeXfer*` class names belong to the later steps: #62243 keeps `mooncake_connector.py` as the compatibility shim until `connector.py` exists in S5.

## Follow-ups

- The rest of the split is S2-S5 of #62243: `bootstrap.py` and `scheduler.py`, the push-side geometry moving into the existing `transfer_plan.py`, the worker becoming `base_worker.py` + `push_worker.py` + `pull_worker.py`, and the facades moving to `connector.py`. Each step waits for an in-flight PR to merge first: #57309 for the spec classification, #61974 for the pull connector, #57529 for the failure ledger, #56939 for metrics.
- The runtime half of the wire contract is the compatibility hash from #61974, which this plan moves into `metadata.py`. The two wire protocols stay separate; unifying them would change the format.
- Two `str` aliases are the only reason `protocol.py` depends on `metadata.py`, and `metadata.py` pulls in `v1.base` and `kv_connector/utils.py`. Whether those aliases belong in a leaf module is a layout decision for #62243 or #57373, not something to change inside a move.
- `mooncake_connector.py` keeps its `mooncake_` prefix and the `MooncakeXfer*` class names until S5, when `connector.py` exists and the old path becomes an `__all__` shim.
- Two PRs land after this one and both touch the same package. #53205 changes the wire: each `req_blocks` entry gains a third element and `remote_dcp_size` / `remote_block_size` are appended, so the schema tables here and the compatibility hash are edited in whichever PR merges second. #62504 adds a second execution shape of the WRITE path, so S3 and S4 keep `transfer_plan.py`, `push_worker.py` and `scheduler.py` subclassable rather than closed.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- No other open PR moves these definitions; no open PR references #62243 in its body.
- #57309 touches the same file only to swap the spec-classification helpers to framework spec kinds; it moves no metadata or wire struct, and none of its hunks overlap the renamed lines.
- #61974 adds `mooncake_pull_connector.py`, `transfer_plan.py` and `compat.py`; its pull wire structs, planning module and compatibility hash stay with that PR and are not absorbed here.

@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import msgspec
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.protocol import (
+    MooncakeXferMetadata,
+    MooncakeXferResponse,
+    MooncakeXferResponseStatus,
+)
+
+# The wire contract of the push protocol, stated once. Field order, wire name,
+# type and default are what the peer decodes against, so a deliberate change to
+# any of them is meant to show up here as an edit of this table, and an
+# accidental one as a failure. The runtime counterpart is the compatibility
+# hash in metadata.py, which refuses a pair whose wire differs.
+EXPECTED_METADATA_SCHEMA = [
+    ("remote_hostname", "str", "required"),
+    ("remote_port", "int", "required"),
+    ("remote_tp_size", "int", "required"),
+    ("remote_tp_rank", "int", "required"),
+    ("req_blocks", "dict[str, tuple[str, list[list[int]]]]", "required"),
+    ("kv_caches_base_addr", "list[int]", "required"),
+    ("block_lens", "list[int]", "required"),
+    ("kv_block_lens", "list[int]", "required"),
+    ("registered_layer_names", "list[str]", "factory=list"),
+    ("registered_layer_indices", "list[int]", "factory=list"),
+    ("registered_group_indices", "list[int]", "factory=list"),
+    ("registered_shared_group_ids", "list[list[int]]", "factory=list"),
+    ("registered_row_offsets", "list[int]", "factory=list"),
+    ("remote_pp_size", "int", "default=1"),
+    ("layout_id", "int", "default=0"),
+]
+
+EXPECTED_RESPONSE_SCHEMA = [
+    ("status", "MooncakeXferResponseStatus", "required"),
+    ("ok_reqs", "list[str] | None", "default=None"),
+    ("err_reqs", "list[str] | None", "default=None"),
+    ("err_msg", "str | None", "default=None"),
+    ("layout_id", "int", "default=0"),
+]
+
+
+def _default_of(field: msgspec.structs.FieldInfo) -> str:
+    if field.required:
+        return "required"
+    if field.default_factory is not msgspec.NODEFAULT:
+        return f"factory={field.default_factory.__name__}"
+    return f"default={field.default!r}"
+
+
+def _type_name(tp: object) -> str:
+    # Plain classes render as "<class 'str'>"; subscripts and unions read best
+    # as their own repr.
+    return tp.__name__ if isinstance(tp, type) else str(tp)
+
+
+def _schema(struct: type[msgspec.Struct]) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
+    return [
+        (field.name, _type_name(field.type), _default_of(field))
+        for field in msgspec.structs.fields(struct)
+    ]
+
+
+def test_xfer_metadata_schema_is_unchanged():
+    assert _schema(MooncakeXferMetadata) == EXPECTED_METADATA_SCHEMA
+
+
+def test_xfer_response_schema_is_unchanged():
+    assert _schema(MooncakeXferResponse) == EXPECTED_RESPONSE_SCHEMA
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "struct", [MooncakeXferMetadata, MooncakeXferResponse], ids=lambda c: c.__name__
+)
+def test_wire_configuration_is_unchanged(struct: type[msgspec.Struct]):
+    config = struct.__struct_config__
+    # Both messages omit defaults on the wire, and neither is tagged or
+    # array-encoded, so decoding depends on the field names in the tables above.
+    assert config.omit_defaults is True
+    assert config.tag is None

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from enum import IntEnum
+
+import msgspec
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.metadata import (
+    ReqId,
+    TransferId,
+)
+
+
+class MooncakeXferMetadata(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    remote_hostname: str
+    remote_port: int
+    remote_tp_size: int
+    remote_tp_rank: int
+    req_blocks: dict[ReqId, tuple[TransferId, list[list[int]]]]
+    kv_caches_base_addr: list[int]
+    block_lens: list[int]
+    kv_block_lens: list[int]
+    registered_layer_names: list[str] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    registered_layer_indices: list[int] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    registered_group_indices: list[int] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    # Parallel to registered regions. Each entry is the groups that share
+    # that region. Empty means the peer did not send the field.
+    registered_shared_group_ids: list[list[int]] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    # Byte offset of each registered view from its block row. -1 means the
+    # peer did not send the field, so the run must not be promoted.
+    registered_row_offsets: list[int] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    remote_pp_size: int = 1
+    # Random per register_kv_caches, so ids never repeat across restarts.
+    # 0 means the peer sends the layout on every pull.
+    layout_id: int = 0
+
+
+class MooncakeXferResponseStatus(IntEnum):
+    # Transfer finished
+    FINISH = 0
+    # Continue to receive
+    CONTINUE = 1
+    # Something wrong, see err_msg
+    ERROR = 2
+    # P does not hold the layout for this layout_id; resend it.
+    # Only sent for pulls with a nonzero layout_id and no layout.
+    LAYOUT_MISS = 3
+
+
+class MooncakeXferResponse(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    status: MooncakeXferResponseStatus
+    ok_reqs: list[ReqId] | None = None
+    err_reqs: list[ReqId] | None = None
+    err_msg: str | None = None
+    # The pull's layout_id once P holds that layout. D omits the layout only
+    # after seeing it, so a P that predates this field always gets it.
+    layout_id: int = 0
+
+
+class MooncakeLeaseHeartbeat(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Sent by D to renew P's lease on KV blocks that D has not pulled yet.
+
+    It shares P's side channel with pulls. A pull decodes as a heartbeat with
+    no transfer ids, because msgspec skips the fields it does not know.
+    """
+
+    lease_transfer_ids: list[TransferId] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
